The papers we counted

All 2,877 items behind the paper counts, by year of publication

These are the items classified as public cryptanalysis of the studied assumptions (include = yes, categories A–F and H) that enter the paper counts on the summary page. An item that attacks more than one assumption is split fractionally; the weights shown are the ones the counts use. Labels come from a two-pass AI classifier and have not been checked by a person. Each line under an entry is the classifier's own rationale.

The page is rendered from bibliography.bib (all items), also available per year. Custom fields record the class weights (classes), rubric category, classifier rationale, source databases and whether the item appears in ePrint or DBLP (vetted). Peer-reviewed means the item appeared in a refereed journal or conference (venue quality not assessed). Quantum marks items whose main point is a quantum algorithm or a quantum resource estimate (the classifier's quantum field); everything else is non-quantum. Each work is counted once: a preprint or duplicate record of a counted work is listed with weight 0, and a journal extension of a conference paper counts one third. Borderline and excluded items are in the full export.
